title: Schema-aware PII lineage and retention corrector for analytics
creator: Emma Chen
description:
Problem: Analytics event streams and derived usage metrics currently rely on a mix of hardcoded PII scrubbing heuristics and downstream backfills. When schema evolves or new PII-bearing fields are introduced (nested JSON blobs, ad-hoc metadata), retention enforcement gaps appear: ephemeral exports and derived aggregates can persist PII beyond allowed windows. Existing deletion workflows are heavyweight and hard to target for corrective backfills without risking data integrity or analytic continuity.

Proposal: Implement a Schema-aware PII Lineage & Retention Corrector (SPLIC) service. SPLIC combines (1) a schema-driven PII classifier, (2) immutable lineage tags attached to ingested events, and (3) a retention-corrector backfill engine that performs incremental, idempotent scrubs/rewrites with strong auditability and safe rollback semantics. The goal is to ensure event-level PII is discoverable and enforceable across pipelines and derived artifacts with minimal disruption to analytics consumers.

High-level flow:
1) Ingest-time: leveraging existing Confluent/Kafka ingestion hooks, SPLIC consults the Central Schema Registry to map event fields to types and PII risk (configurable per project/customer). It emits a small set of lineage tags (pii_detected:[fieldnames], schema_version, retention_bucket) into event headers and to a light-weight audit topic.
2) Storage-time: storage systems (raw event lake, OLAP materializations, feature stores) consume lineage tags. When a retention window expires or a manual correction is required, the retention-corrector can target only the events with matching lineage tags + schema_version to minimize blast radius.
3) Backfill/corrector: a distributed job orchestrates safe scrubs — either tokenization, field-level redaction, or tombstone issuance — producing a manifest of changed object IDs and a cryptographic attestation (hash of before/after). Jobs are idempotent and versioned by schema_version so replays are safe.
4) Audit & export: all corrective actions are recorded in an append-only audit ledger (S3+immutable index) for compliance queries and legal reviews. The console exposes a read-only view for ops with links to manifests and PRs.

Why different: SPLIC is schema-first (not purely regex/heuristics), attaches lineage to events to make future corrections targeted and efficient, and emphasizes idempotent, auditable correction rather than large destructive deletes. It supports safe roll-forward and rollback with explicit manifests to satisfy both compliance and analytics continuity requirements.
acceptance_criteria: Ingest hook successfully tags events with schema_version and pii_detected metadata for at least 3 representative event types (console_login, api_request, billing_event)
Retention-corrector can run a non-destructive dry-run that produces a manifest and estimated token-count impact for a selected customer/time-range
A single-field PII backfill (e.g., redact user.email) completes against a test bucket without breaking downstream query schemas and is fully idempotent on retries
Audit ledger contains immutable entries for every corrective action with links to manifest, job run, and responsible engineer and is queryable by retention_bucket and customer_id
Security review sign-off achieved and KMS integration validated for tokenization key rotation
tasks: Design schema mapping table and PII risk levels (privacy team + PM)
Implement ingest-time hook to read Central Schema Registry and emit lineage headers
Extend raw-lake consumer adapters to persist lineage headers into event metadata storage
Build retention-corrector worker with dry-run, apply, and rollback modes
Add manifest format and cryptographic attestation (sha256) to audit ledger
Create Console Ops view for searching manifests and triggering corrective dry-runs
Write integration tests covering nested JSON field redaction and idempotency
Run privacy + security review and remediate findings
implementation_notes: Prefer lightweight lineage headers to avoid inflating event size; store canonical mapping in audit topic instead of duplicating whole event
Use schema_version to scope backfills: corrections only touch events with matching schema_version to avoid accidental scrubs on new formats
Backfills should operate on primary object IDs (event_id, session_id) and produce tombstone manifests consumable by downstream ETL
Tokenization uses envelope encryption with customer-scoped KMS key; store token metadata in a restricted metadata table with access controls
Provide a 'safe mode' flag that runs changes into a shadow prefix (s3://.../shadow/) so downstream consumers can validate before swap
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: Large backfills could overload storage/compute -> Mitigation: rate limit jobs, do progressive windows, and provide cost/impact estimator in dry-run
Risk: Schema drift causing missed PII detection -> Mitigation: daily schema-diff alerts and a QA job that runs a high-recall PII scanner over a sample
Risk: Incorrect redaction breaks dashboards -> Mitigation: shadow rewrites + automated consumer validation and rollback endpoint
Risk: Audit ledger tampering -> Mitigation: append-only S3 manifests with signed attestation and server-side object lock enabled
test_plan: Unit tests for schema mapping and header emission (local schema registry mock)
Integration test: ingest pipeline tagging -> storage -> retention-corrector dry-run -> apply -> verify downstream query results
Load test: run candidate backfill at production-like throughput in staging to validate throttling and job orchestration
Compliance test: produce audit ledger entries and run retention queries to validate manifests are discoverable by customer_id and retention_bucket
